- list 2 of 3Why US-Iran war over Hormuz is threatening the Gulf’s waters
- list 3 of 3The war in the Gulf will have to end in compromise
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded to Cao’s acknowledgement of the damage inflicted on the US facility. “We appreciate the candor of Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao,” the official wrote on X.
“Our powerful Armed Forces did indeed ‘blow the hell out of the 5th Fleet HQ in Bahrain,’ as well as other bases supporting US aggression.”
US bases across the Middle East have come under repeated attack by Iran, raising questions about whether they can be sustained. Iranian strikes overnight on Tuesday also hit the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, known as the Al-Azraq base, damaging multiple US military aircraft.
What do we know about the damage to the US base in Bahrain?
Imagery obtained from open sources indicates the US’s Naval Support Activity (NSA) base in Bahrain sustained heavy damage in retaliatory strikes after the US and Israel launched air attacks across Iran in late February. The base was repeatedly targeted between February and June, according to reports.
The Wall Street Journal, which analysed satellite imagery, social media footage and conducted interviews with service members, concluded that Iranian strikes caused extensive damage which the Pentagon did not immediately acknowledge.
The command centre at the base and at least a dozen other buildings within the facility were hit hard, the investigation found.
Cao said the Navy was evaluating what to do with the base now, including whether to repair it. “I have a task force that’s looking at that,” he told The Epoch Times.
Admiral Daryl Caudle, the Navy’s most senior uniformed officer, said earlier this month that the NSA Bahrain would not resume service “anytime soon” because of the damage it had sustained.
Cao said damage to the base also affected operations involving the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, leaving the crew with “no place for them to pull in”.
The nearly nine-month extended deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East has triggered a mental health crisis among the crew, with some sailors trying to jump overboard, according to US media reports. It finally docked at Laem Chabang, Thailand, earlier this month.
What is the NSA Bahrain?
Until it was heavily damaged, the NSA Bahrain base was home to the US Fifth Fleet and the US Naval Forces Central Command (NAVCENT), serving as the Navy’s main logistics hub in the Middle East.
The base, located a few kilometres from the capital Manama in Juffair, has been described by US news outlets as the nerve centre of US naval operations.
According to its website, the NSA Bahrain provided “services and support to ships at sea, remote sites throughout the region, and military and civilian personnel living in Bahrain”.
The installation was also the primary base in the region for Navy activities during the US military invasion and occupation of Iraq in 2003.
What happened to the US base in Jordan?
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had launched “devastating” missile strikes on US forces stationed at the Al-Azraq base, which hosts US military assets and personnel, overnight on Tuesday.
Missiles “struck the maintenance, preparation, and deployment sites of F-35, F-16, and F-15 fighter jets, as well as their shelters, inflicting heavy damage on the enemy”, the IRGC said in the statement reported by the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
The Jordanian Armed Forces said 18 of 20 missiles had been intercepted, with two falling in “open areas”. US forces fired about 30 Patriot interceptor missiles to counter the missiles, amid reports of depleting stockpiles of US air defence interceptors and other missiles.
However, the strikes still damaged multiple US military aircraft, CBS News reported. One A-10 Thunderbolt, an attack aircraft known as the Warthog, was struck and lost a wing, the news outlet said, citing sources.
Eight F-15s sustained light damage and were put back into service, according to people who spoke to CBS News anonymously because they were not authorised to speak publicly.
The Iranian strike on the base in Jordan was carried out after the US attacked five Iranian tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz, in retaliation for Iran targeting a US Navy warship.
How important is the Jordanian base to the US?
The Muwaffaq Salti Air Base near Al-Azraq is located nearly 100km (62 miles) northeast of Amman. Its official name is a tribute to a Jordanian fighter pilot, Lieutenant Muwaffaq Salti, who was killed in combat with Israel in 1966 in the Battle of as-Samu.
The sprawling base, which has two runways, makes it an important asset for the US – and a target for Iran.
Tehran has claimed strikes on the Al-Azraq base more than 10 times between March and September. On June 10, the IRGC said its long-range missiles had destroyed several targets at the Al-Azraq airbase, including hangars and command centres. However, authorities in the countries targeted said all projectiles were intercepted without casualties.
In the following weeks, Iran claimed to have hit the Al-Azraq base multiple times, inflicting heavy damage to US assets there.
On July 17, Iran said it had hit US military aircraft stationed at the Al-Azraq base with ballistic missiles and drones, claiming to have destroyed several refuelling aircraft and fighter jets.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) later confirmed that two US service members had been “killed in action” in the Iranian attack, while one was missing and four were injured.
What other US military assets have been damaged in the Middle East?
According to a May report from the US Congressional Research Service, 42 US military aircraft had already been lost or damaged in the conflict by that time.
Since the Iran war began with US-Israeli strikes in February, 18 US service members have been killed and more than 800 have been injured.
Iran has targeted key US facilities in eight countries in the Middle East since the start of the war. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed the Middle East was no longer a “safe place” for US bases.
Images and videos analysed by the BBC in June showed that Iran had damaged at least 20 US military sites since the start of the war, causing millions of dollars of damage.
Iranian strikes heavily hit US refuelling and surveillance aircraft at Prince Sultan Airbase in Saudi Arabia, as well as fuel storage bunkers, aircraft hangars and troop accommodation at the Ali Al Salem Airbase and Camp Arifjan in Kuwait, BBC reported.
Three state-of-the-art anti-ballistic missile battery systems, which cost about $1bn each to manufacture, were also damaged at the Al Ruwais and Al Sader airbases in the UAE and Muwaffaq Salti Airbase in Jordan.

EU pledges €6.1bn for Ukraine, including aid for Patriot interceptors
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:40:18 UTC
19:40:18 KST

Brussels is trying to persuade EU countries that still have Patriot interceptors in their national stockpiles to donate them to Ukraine and replace them at a later stage with deliveries scheduled for 2027.
The European Union is set to provide Ukraine with €6.1 billion in additional assistance to help the war-weary country purchase military equipment, notably the Patriot interceptors badly needed to shoot down Russia's devastating ballistic missiles.
The funding, announcedon Friday, will come from the bloc's €90 billion support loan, which reserves €28.3 billion for military aid and €16.7 billion for budget aid this year.
The loan's "Made In Europe" requirement will be lifted to procure Patriots, which are made in the United States, and drones, which depend on Chinese components.
The newly allocated €6.1 billion represents the final allocation under the €28.3 billion envelope. Payments are being made in gradual instalments after Brussels checks and verifies the contracts that Kyiv signs with private companies.
So far, €8.35 billion in defence funding has been wired.
"The Ukrainian military edge depends on the rapid availability of critical products in the required quantities and within very short time frames," Andrius Kubilius, the European Commissioner for Defence, said at a press conference.
"Accelerating EU deliveries through de-stocking, reprioritising orders and ramping up production remains crucial."
The news comes as allies race to supply Ukraine with air defence systems as Russia escalates its bombing campaign, including through jet-powered drones, ahead of a winter that EU officials expect to be the harshest yet of the war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy estimates his army will need about 300 Patriot interceptors to make it through the winter safely.
The scarcity of PAC-3 interceptors, made by US defence giant Lockheed Martin, has severely constrained Kyiv's ability to repel Russia's ballistic missiles effectively. Moscow has exploited the weakness to double down on lethal airstrikes.
The war in the Middle East has compounded the backlog in production chains, which was burdensome to begin with. A single PAC-3 interceptor has a 24-month manufacturing lead time and a price tag of roughly $4 million (€3.45 billion).
In a bid to speed things up, Brussels is seeking to convince member states that still have Patriot interceptors in their national stockpiles to donate them to Ukraine and replace them later on with the deliveries scheduled for 2027 – in other words, a swap.
"The Ukrainians, as we understand, will put all the efforts now to have those interceptors as much as possible before winter," Kubilius said.
"NATO is also very intensively working on that," he added, referring to the alliance's PURL programme, which mobilises US-made weaponry for Ukraine.
"I hope that that will be really realised in an effective way."
Kubilius spoke to the press after the first meeting of the EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance, which intends to combine the former's industrial scale with the latter's innovative prowess to foster joint production of unmanned aerial vehicles.
The meeting gathered 18 companies from the bloc and 9 from Ukraine, he said.
The alliance builds upon the EU-Ukraine Drone Deal signed in July.

Delays once again: how the next court hearings in the Odrex doctors’ case did (not) take place
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
13:40:06 EEST
19:40:06 KST

Delays once again: how the next court hearings in the Odrex doctors’ case did (not) take place
Kyiv • UNN
The court deemed the reasons for Rusakov’s lawyers’ absence unjustified and plans to обратиться to the disciplinary commission
At the Kyivskyi District Court of Odesa, the trial in the case against Odrex clinic doctors Vitaliy Rusakov and Maryna Bielotserkovska was due to continue on September 10 and 11. They are accused of medical negligence which, according to the investigation, could have caused the death of businessman Adnan Kivan. However, the hearings did not take place, UNN writes.
The lawyers for the accused, Vitaliy Rusakov, filed a motion to postpone the hearings scheduled for September 10 and 11, as they were due to participate in other court hearings scheduled for the same dates.
The judge found the reasons for the postponement unjustified and said that he would send a ruling to the Bar's Qualification and Disciplinary Commission seeking disciplinary action against the doctor's defense lawyers.
However, the court hearings did not take place. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for September 16.
逃避司法：Odrex 医生案件的审理如何被拖延，以及是否正在准备新的陷阱10.09.26, 13:12 • 53569 views
We remind you that during the September 10 hearing, the court was to hear the objections of Bielotserkovska's defense to the prosecution's evidence. At previous hearings, Rusakov's defense had already presented its arguments.
The court is currently at one of the key stages of the proceedings – examination of the evidence. During this stage, the court must assess the medical records, conclusions of forensic medical examinations, clinical protocols, and other materials on which the prosecution's case is based. The court will subsequently hear the conclusions of an independent medical expert.
Rusakov and Bielotserkovska are accused under Part 1 of Article 140 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine – improper performance of professional duties by medical workers. According to the investigation, after the operation the medical workers may have failed to prescribe Adnan Kivan the necessary antibacterial therapy and may have responded inadequately to postoperative complications. According to the conclusions of the forensic medical examination, this could have led to the development of sepsis and the patient's death. The accused do not admit their guilt.
The actions of the defense and the time factor in the case involving Odrex doctors
The trial has already been accompanied for many months by numerous attempts to delay the proceedings; in particular, hearings did not take place because lawyers failed to appear, and were repeatedly postponed due to procedural motions by the defense. The defendants' lawyers also заявляли challenges to judges, initiated a change of jurisdiction, and petitioned for the indictment to be returned to the prosecutor. As a result, after the proceedings were transferred from the Prymorskyi to the Kyivskyi District Court of Odesa, the preparatory proceedings had to be conducted again, and when the court finally began considering the case on its merits, the defense lawyers began ignoring the hearings.
Doctor Rusakov is also actively putting pressure on the judge, in particular by publishing memes featuring his photograph. And when the court extended his suspension from his position at the Odrex clinic so that he could not communicate with witnesses, Rusakov appealed to his patients, urging them to complain to the High Council of Justice because they were unable to see him for appointments. Large numbers of identical complaints can create psychological pressure on a judge, even if they subsequently prove unfounded. In such a situation, the judge is forced to spend time explaining and responding to each complaint.
The lawyers interviewed by UNN did not rule out that the totality of such procedural actions could be a defense strategy aimed at having the case closed because the statute of limitations expires. In particular, Denys Neviadomskyi, president of the All-Ukrainian Association of Retired Judges, emphasized that every unjustified postponement of a trial brings the criminal proceedings closer to being closed on the grounds that the statute of limitations has expired, which would make it impossible to establish justice in the case concerning Adnan Kivan's death.
The time factor plays a significant role in this case. Since Adnan Kivan died at the end of October 2024, and the charges were brought under Part 1 of Article 140 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine, the three-year statute of limitations provided for such cases will expire in the autumn of 2027. By that time, the judgment must not only have been issued by the court of first instance but must also have become legally binding.
Thus, the defense’s constant procedural "maneuvers" may raise the question of whether a fair court decision will be delivered or whether the case will be closed once the prescribed time limits have expired.

Why North Korea's Kim Jong Un doesn't need a US deal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:40:00 UTC
19:40:00 KST

Why North Korea's Kim Jong Un doesn't need a US deal
September 11, 2026
In August, US President Donald Trump revived a charm offensive aimed at Pyongyang by drastically scaling back joint US military exercises with South Korea and heaping praise on North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.The US president said the North Korean dictator "has always treated me with great respect."
North Korea's response to Trump's overtures has been markedly less enthusiastic, ranging from firing a barrage of missiles to publicly denying Trump's claims that Kim has responded "very positively" to a request for talks.
This week, as the US and South Korea, along with Japan, kicked off a five-day military drill, there was no mention of any pullback from Washington, nor any sign of diplomatic progress with Pyongyang.
Instead, Kim on Monday commissioned a naval destroyer, while again emphasizing North Korea must establish a "powerful and reliable nuclear war deterrent" and strengthen "maritime defense." Kim also said North Korea would soon unveil a "significant" naval advancement.
No urgency for deal with US
Unlike the summit diplomacy of Trump's first term, Kim's dismissive stance comes at a time when North Korea has alternatives to a grand bargain with the United States.
"For Kim, the stakes are simply lower than they were in 2019. There is no longer the same sense of urgency in Pyongyang to get back to the negotiating table with Washington," Joon Ha Park, a correspondent at Korea Risk Group in Seoul, told DW.
"North Korea now has a treaty-based alliance with Moscow and is drawing closer to Beijing, while its military capabilities have expanded significantly. That's why a single reduction in ROK-US military exercises is not enough for Pyongyang to be swayed," he added, referring to military ties between South Korea and the US.
Kim rides high
Park agrees that Kim is arguably in his strongest position since taking power in 2011.
Just six years ago, amid crippling sanctions and the coronavirus pandemic, an emotional Kim stood at the lectern marking the 75th anniversary of the Korean Workers' Party and expressed regret for having failed the North Korean people.
Fast forward to today, and North Korea's economy appears to be on a stronger footing. Estimates released last year by South Korea's central bank showed the economy expanded by 3.7% in 2024, its fastest rate of growth in eight years.
Kim has brought North Korea closer to Russia and China than the traditionally isolated country has been in decades. This week, both Moscow and Beijing sent messages marking North Korea's 78th founding anniversary and praising the strategic importance of their deepening partnerships with Pyongyang.
Kim's recent spate of good fortune began in 2023, after a summit with Vladimir Putin in Russia's far east. The meeting opened the door for North Korea delivering arms to help Russia fight the Ukraine war, with Moscow sending back aid.
Since then, Pyongyang has heavily ramped up industrial military production, buoyed by fresh financing that skirts international sanctions.
Beijing responds to the Russia-North Korea alliance
China, North Korea's traditional benefactor, quickly took notice of the growing alignment between Moscow and Pyongyang, but initially kept its distance.
"The war in Ukraine has opened up a crucial lifeline for the [North Korean] regime, delivering weapons, ammunitions and soldiers to Russia in return for cash, foodstuff and ostensibly advanced military technology," Alexander Lipke, policy fellow with the Asia Program at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR), told DW.
"These warming ties with Russia have also alarmed China, which is also actively attempting to cement its position as Pyongyang's preeminent partner," he added.
By 2025, Russia and North Korea's ever closer ties forced Beijing to pivot and showcase its leading role among the three countries. In September that year, Kim was invited to the "Victory Day" celebrations in Beijing, and for the first time, stood publicly on stage alongside Xi and Putin.
For a regime known for its international isolation, Kim standing shoulder to shoulder with the leaders of Russia and China was a major milestone. This was again the case when in June 2026, Xi's first foreign trip of the year took him to Pyongyang.
Denuclearization off the table?
Notably, any mention of "denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula" was omitted from communiques following these high-level meetings, despite the phrase previously being part of boilerplate diplomatic language from Beijing and Moscow.
This diplomatic softening comes as North Korea aggressively takes steps to ramp up its nuclear program. In February 2026, Kim said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "irreversible," while calling for the country's nuclear force to be expanded. Recent analysis of satellite imagery suggests increased activity at known North Korean nuclear sites.
Pyongyang has also insisted on US recognition as a nuclear weapons state as a precondition for any talks with Washington, while emphasizing that any future summits must omit language on "denuclearization."
North Korea is estimated to have nearly 60 nuclear warheads, which is double the 20-30 warheads Pyongyang is thought to have possessed during Trump's last diplomatic episode with Kim in 2018 and 2019.
"North Korea is no longer looking for talks centered on denuclearization or even traditional arms control. It increasingly wants recognition, implicitly or otherwise, as a nuclear weapons state," said Park from the Korea Risk Group.
He added that any Trump summit without denuclearization included as part of the official agenda "could be portrayed by Pyongyang both domestically and internationally as implicit US acceptance of North Korea's nuclear status."
Sanctions don't matter anymore?
Since its first nuclear test in 2006, North Korea has been subject to a strict sanctions regime, with the UN Security Council having passed nine sanctions resolutions aimed at restricting exports, along with asset freezes.
The last package was passed in 2017. At that point, it was combined with pressure and fiery rhetoric from the first Trump administration, raising tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Kim was under heavy economic pressure and seeking sanctions relief in return for concessions on his nuclear program. But that moment has now long passed.
"North Korea's diplomatic situation has vastly improved, reducing the pressure to come to the table to cut a deal with the US," said Lipke, adding that "independent sanctions enforcement has widely collapsed," with Russia and China no longer actively pursuing their non-proliferation stance of previous decades.
Lipke said North Korea no longer needs a bargain with the US regarding sanctions relief in return for partial denuclearization.
"But the bargain now on the table could potentially be much larger for North Korea, a freeze in nuclear development in exchange for the recognition by the US as a de-facto nuclear state in front of the whole world."

Biotechnology at scale: Europe’s next competitiveness test
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:39:07 UTC
19:39:07 KST

Biotechnology at scale: 
 Europe’s next competitiveness test 
Key findings
- Biotechnology is increasingly important to Europe’s healthcare, food security, industrial decarbonization and strategic autonomy, generating €75.16 billion in gross value added in 2022. The EU retains major scientific strengths, but struggles to translate research into companies, manufacturing capacity, commercial value and broad societal benefits. Three factors will determine whether Europe can close this innovation translation gap.
- First, regulatory simplification will need to extend across the innovation pathway. Biotechnology increasingly cuts across rules governing medicines, clinical trials, data, agriculture, intellectual property and trade. The European Biotech Act seeks to improve coordination, but its impact will depend on whether implementation reduces fragmentation across Member States rather than adding new structures to an already complex regulatory landscape.
- Second, scientific strength must be matched by the capacity to scale. Europe remains comparatively weak in late-stage financing, attracting only 7 percent of global health-biotech venture capital, compared with 14 percent for China and 63 percent for the United States. Specialized manufacturing, testing infrastructure, high-quality data and AI are increasingly critical to commercialization. BioTechEU and the European Competitiveness Fund could strengthen these conditions, but Europe will capture limited value from its research if companies continue to finance, manufacture and scale elsewhere.
- Third, successful innovation depends on access as well as commercialization. Advanced therapies demonstrate that EU authorization does not guarantee patient access: of 32 ATMPs authorized since 2009, seven have been withdrawn and two were not renewed. Manufacturing, reimbursement and treatment capacity remain important constraints. NGTs present a parallel challenge: regulatory predictability alone will not ensure uptake without workable intellectual property and licensing conditions, financing, farmer and supply-chain acceptance, and access for smaller actors. How widely biotechnology’s benefits are distributed will also shape public legitimacy.
- These factors point to three possible trajectories toward 2035. Coordinated regulation, investment and industrial capacity could reinforce Europe’s scientific strengths and support biotechnology leadership. Partial progress could preserve research excellence without closing the scale-up gap. Weaker investment conditions and policy coherence could instead accelerate the movement of capital, companies, talent and production elsewhere.
- Europe’s biotechnology challenge is therefore not primarily one of scientific capability, but of translation: connecting research to regulation, capital, industrial scale and access. The European Biotech Act will be an early test of whether Europe can build those connections strongly enough to retain the economic and societal value of the innovation it creates.

LONDON, September 11. /TASS/. Powerful states once again threaten the UK’s security after decades, while the danger of terrorism persists, MI5 Director General Ken McCallum said, urging the country to act.
He recalled a metaphor used by former CIA Director James Woolsey at a US congressional hearing in 1993, when he said the West had defeated a dragon but now faced numerous poisonous snakes. The dragon represented the Soviet Union, while the snakes stood for non-state threats, including terrorist groups. "We now face the worst of both worlds: dragons are back, but snakes persist," the MI5 chief wrote in a column published in The Independent marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks in the US.
"The terrorist threat now sits alongside strategic national security threats posed by capable States," McCallum wrote, without specifying which countries he meant.
"This is my call to arms after 25 years: government, business, academia, and the public must treat national security not as the specialist concern of a handful of agencies, but as a shared national endeavor," he said, urging the country not to wait for the next shock and to prepare for future threats rather than yesterday’s battles. He also argued that the situation demands new laws and intelligence methods.

The European Commission has approved an additional €6.1 billion loan for Ukraine to purchase various defense products. In particular, this concerns a package that enables Ukraine to procure PAC-3 missiles for Patriot systems, as well as finance Ukrainian drones and their components. This is reported on the European Commission’s website, UNN reports.
Details
Today, the European Commission approved the allocation of an additional €6.1 billion to Ukraine for the purchase of various defense capabilities in the fields of air and missile defense, ammunition, drones, and electronic warfare systems. This urgently needed funding will help strengthen Ukraine’s ability to withstand the ongoing intensification of Russian strikes with ballistic missiles and drones
The funds will be used to purchase defense products from both EU companies and Ukrainian companies. The decision also gives Ukraine the opportunity to purchase PAC-3 missiles for Patriot systems.
The aid package, financed במסגרת the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan, provides for five exceptions to the standard conditions for the provision of assistance: three for Ukrainian-made drones and components whose cost exceeds the established thresholds, and two for U.S.-made equipment, including PAC-3 missiles, including through the NATO-coordinated PURL mechanism.
The European Commission added that this year it has already allocated €8.35 billion to finance Ukraine’s defense, and additional funds will be allocated soon.
We remind you
The European Commission approved Ukraine’s application to purchase missiles for Patriot air defense systems במסגרת the Ukraine Support Loan. The application concerns approximately €3.2 billion to strengthen Ukraine’s air defense.

Transparency data: Military court centres court listings
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
11:36:53 BST
19:36:53 KST

Military court centres court listings
Court listings for the military court centres.
Documents
Details
In line with the government’s transparency and open data initiative, the Military Court Service is to publish the court listings for the military court centres.
Each court listing covers the next one or two week assize period. This will be published on the internet by the last working day in advance of the assize period.
In addition to this, the court listings are published using digital signage technology within the reception areas of both military court centres.
Please be aware that the court listings are subject to change after publication, if you wish to find out more please contact the relevant military court centre. Details can be found at the bottom of each court listing.

Cong v Cong: Tharoor rebuffs Chidambaram's view on Brics, hails summit's 'diplomatic convening power'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:36:05 UTC
19:36:05 KST

Tharoor versus Chidambaram on BRICS. Photo credit: ANI
NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has backed the Brics summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, breaking ranks with party colleague P Chidambaram, who has questioned whether recent Brics meetings have delivered tangible benefits.Defending the grouping’s relevance, Tharoor said it gives India a platform to engage with the Global South and a “diplomatic convening power”, bringing together countries that collectively account for a large share of the world’s population and economy.Speaking to news agency PTI on Thursday, The Congress MP said the expanded Brics grouping represents a significant share of the global population and economy.
“First of all, we're providing an important platform for the Global South. You know, the Global South is over 100 countries, but here we have 11 key players from the Global South who collectively represent much of the diversity of views, as well as the range of countries that we are essentially chairing on this particular occasion. This grouping, the 11 Brics countries, represents a majority of the world's population and 41 per cent of global GDP", Tharoor said.
Tharoor also highlighted the diplomatic significance of India hosting the summit, with leaders beginning to arrive in New Delhi.“It's not a small matter; it's something that has to be taken very seriously by the rest of the world,” he said.Tharoor also pointed to the diplomatic value of hosting leaders from across the grouping and its partner countries. “Secondly, of course, having a dozen heads of state and government, not only members of Brics but also some observers coming at presidential and prime ministerial level, is a matter of great prestige for us. It shows a certain diplomatic convening power, which has value in and of itself on the global stage.”His comments came after Chidambaram questioned the outcomes of recent Brics meetings. Speaking to ANI on Wednesday, Chidambaram said, “I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results.”“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.The remarks triggered a political response from the BJP, which accused the Congress of questioning an event that it said reflected India’s growing global standing.Senior Congress leader and former external affairs minister Salman Khurshid, meanwhile, urged the party to view Chidambaram’s remarks as a caution rather than criticism.“If Chidambaram is giving a word of caution, we should take it in the right spirit,” Khurshid told ANI. “And if it's taken in the right spirit, we may have a better outcome from this summit.”However, in another video, Tharoor addressed the difficulties in India-China ties, saying they “have come entirely from one side". He also cited the Galwan tragedy, border tensions, visa issues and trade leverage and stressed that a “self-respecting India” would stand up for itself and called for greater flexibility, understanding and friendship."So yes, the bilateral relationship, the bilateral meeting, is potentially very important, but what we're looking for is a little more flexibility, understanding, and friendship coming from the Chinese side than they've shown us in the last six years", Tharoor added.
Brics currently comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE. Together, the 11 members account for around 49.5 per cent of the global population, 40 per cent of global GDP and 26 per cent of global trade.The 18th Brics Summit will be held in New Delhi on September 12-13, with Russian president Vladimir Putin, Chinese president Xi Jinping and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian among the key leaders attending.Putin arrived in New Delhi on Friday and is scheduled to meet prime minister Narendra Modi ahead of the summit, as India seeks to use its Brics chairship to push for greater cooperation. With the summit set to begin on Saturday, the focus will now be on whether New Delhi can turn its diplomatic convening power into concrete outcomes.
Subhadra Srivastava is a journalist with The Times of India, covering geopolitics, international and national affairs. With over three years of experience, she focuses on national and global developments, conflict, diplomacy and their impact on India. Her work combines breaking news with in-depth analysis, offering readers context and clarity on the stories shaping the world.

Mexico, Washington sprint toward bilateral trade deal before US elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:36:04 UTC
19:36:04 KST

Mexico, Washington sprint toward bilateral trade deal before US elections
MEXICO CITY/WASHINGTON, Sept 11 - Mexico and the United States are racing to reach a bilateral trade deal before the U.S. midterm elections in less than eight weeks, according to six sources in both countries familiar with the talks, an effort made more urgent by the collapse of Canadian negotiations with Washington.
"We both want to reach a deal before the midterms," said one Mexico-based source, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss private talks.
The negotiations are aimed at striking an interim bilateral bargain under which Mexico could win relief from some U.S. tariffs while addressing U.S. demands on areas including automotive content and Chinese investment.
While no formal deadline exists, officials in both countries see political benefits in reaching a deal before the November 3 elections when U.S. President Donald Trump's Republican Party risks losing control of Congress. An accord would enable both leaders to tout a win as they face domestic political challenges.
"Time is of the essence for the Mexican government," said the Mexican source, citing concerns over a weak economy and falling credit ratings on its debt. The source added that Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum's administration, which this week presented its 2027 budget, views a U.S. trade deal as critical to reassuring markets and investors.
A spokesperson for Mexico's economy ministry said, "There are no specific deadlines at this time," stressing the government's ongoing commitment to dialogue with Washington.
The U.S. Trade Representative and White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
MEXICO CONCILIATORY
Mexico's push to reach a deal comes after trade talks between the United States and Canada collapsed last month, plunging the longtime allies into a bitter tariff dispute.
Washington on Tuesday banned imports of a broad swath of Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products, and Ottawa has vowed to match U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar.
The collapse of Canada's talks has reinforced Mexico's strategy of avoiding direct confrontation with Washington, betting that cooperation will yield tariff relief.
The Mexican source described the country's approach as "play nice and continue to cooperate." Mexico sends more than 80% of its exports to its northern neighbor.
Reflecting the intensified pace, U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick met virtually with Sheinbaum on Thursday about trade.
The meeting, originally scheduled in person, came less than two weeks after Sheinbaum proposed legislation giving the government new powers to review and block foreign acquisitions of Mexican companies.
The measure, which would create an investment-screening regime similar to those in the United States and Canada, is widely seen as a response to U.S. pressure for closer scrutiny of Chinese investment.
The U.S.-Mexico talks are being framed as an effort to reach an interim bilateral deal while issues with the three-country USMCA pact including Canada are negotiated.
That agreement was thrown into uncertainty in July when the U.S. did not agree to renew it for another 16 years. The accord remains in effect, subject to annual review, but the Trump administration has used the process to seek additional concessions from Canada and Mexico.
BEST FRENEMIES
Officials in both Mexico and Canada, which have long been uneasy allies, have publicly stressed their commitment to preserving a trilateral agreement. But some Mexican officials privately argue Mexico should not sacrifice its own interests to secure a deal for Canada.
The race for a U.S.-Mexico deal may have additional strategic dimensions. One auto industry source said the Trump administration aims to isolate Ottawa by reaching a deal with Mexico before major new Canadian tariffs take effect on January 1.
A U.S.-Mexico deal could also bring down consumer prices in the United States and deliver a "political win" for the Trump administration, said Diego Marroquin Bitar, an expert on North American trade who also works as a consultant. "They could argue it was Canada's fault they didn't reach an agreement."
OBSTACLES REMAIN
A major hurdle in any interim trade deal is the so-called Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum, automobiles and auto parts. Under those national security tariffs, Mexican and Canadian steel exported to the U.S. face tariffs of 50%, while vehicles are subject to a 25% duty.
Trump has since negotiated lower auto tariffs for other trading partners, including 15% for Japan, the European Union and South Korea, and 10% for Britain, leaving some vehicles from those countries facing lower duties than cars shipped from Mexico and Canada.
Before negotiations collapsed last month, Canada appeared close to a breakthrough with Washington on Section 232 tariffs and other trade issues, raising hopes Mexico could quickly secure similar terms.
Several automakers believe Washington could ultimately offer Mexico the same framework discussed with Canada: a 15% tariff on vehicle imports, plus an additional reduction for U.S. content, bringing the effective tariff rate to around 7%.
In return, Mexico is expected to give ground on U.S. demands for greater American content in vehicles, particularly engines, electronics and software, a second Mexico-based source said.
While Mexico opposes explicit U.S. content requirements, "that doesn't mean it won't be working on something to help increase the U.S. content," the source said, adding that the final shape of such a compromise is "the big question." REUTERS

Taiwan sports ministry orders gymnastics secretary-general fired over missed championship spots
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:35:43 UTC
19:35:43 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The sports ministry on Friday ordered the Chinese Taipei Gymnastics Association to remove its secretary-general and apologize for mishandling replacement eligibility for the 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships, causing two athletes to miss their chance to compete.
The ministry stated the case had materially affected the athletes’ rights to compete and that the association’s explanations, accountability measures, and handling of the incident had failed to meet its governance responsibilities. After holding another meeting Friday to demand an explanation, the ministry said it would initiate procedures under Article 43 of the National Sports Act and remove the secretary-general.
Officials contacted the association Thursday to demand an immediate investigation and accountability but received no concrete response. At a meeting Friday, the association’s chairperson attended while the secretary-general did not, and officials failed to fully explain the decision-making process or responsibilities.
The association was ordered to submit a full review of the case and establish procedures for handling replacement eligibility and emergency notifications for international competitions. Future notices affecting athletes’ competition rights must be immediately shared with athletes, coaches, and relevant selection and training units, it said.
The ministry said sports organizations exist to promote sports and support athletes, and those responsible would be held accountable under the law. It said the measures would not affect other athletes’ training, selection, or participation in international competitions.
World Gymnastics notified the association on Aug. 20 that Pingtung gymnasts Pan Tsai-chen (潘采宸) and Lee Chia-wei (李佳蔚) had obtained replacement spots for the world championships in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, per CNA. Pan had a spot in the floor exercise, while Lee had one in the uneven bars.
The association declined the spots that afternoon, citing insufficient time to complete required administrative procedures. DPP Legislator Hsu Fu-kuei (徐富癸) said the response deadline was still more than 12 hours away and questioned whether the secretary-general had authority to decide without consulting the athletes, coaches, or selection committee.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The campaign of KMT Changhua County magistrate candidate Wei Ping-cheng (魏平政) declined Friday to comment on whether New Taipei Deputy Mayor Liu Ho-jan (劉和然) could chair the campaign, saying Wei is still waiting for Changhua County Magistrate Wang Hui-mei (王惠美) to take the helm.
KMT Vice Chair Li Chien-lung (李乾龍) said Thursday that Liu would serve as chief policy director for Wei's campaign, adding that Liu had volunteered to assist, per China Times. When asked whether Liu would chair the campaign, Li said the campaign was still "waiting for him.”

He emphasized that assisting the county's development did not require an official position, adding that he could help with policy discussions and campaigning.

KMT Changhua County Branch Chair Hsiao Ching-tien (蕭景田) said he needed to ask both Li and Liu about the proposal, but still hoped to see Wang take charge of Wei's campaign, per UDN.
Despite the KMT's efforts to involve Wang, she has continued to distance herself from Wei's campaign. After missing the establishment of Wei's campaign headquarters, Wang posted Thursday on Facebook thanking the Cabinet for supporting policy proposals and tagging local lawmakers in the post, per Tai Sounds.
Wang specifically stressed that county governance should be bipartisan and that the next magistrate would need to continue her work, per Mirror Media. Her comments, along with her tagging of DPP lawmaker and magistrate candidate Chen Su-yueh (陳素月), sparked strong backlash from KMT supporters.

In related news, Wei announced that he would seek to file a lawsuit over attacks targeting a video featuring his daughter that was displayed at his campaign headquarters, per UDN. He said that although he has always supported freedom of speech, sexual attacks and bullying crossed the boundary of reasonable criticism.
The KMT also expressed support for Wei and his family, saying campaign attacks should be directed at politicians rather than their family members, per Tai Sounds.

Houthis seize strategic Perim Island in Bab el-Mandab Strait, Dhubab city
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:35:31 UTC
19:35:31 KST

Mohammed Sameai and Rania Abushamala
11 September 2026•Update: 11 September 2026
Houthi fighters seized the strategic Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the city of Dhubab in the western Taiz province on Friday, a Yemeni government military source told Anadolu.
The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the Houthis had taken control of the island, known in Arabic as Mayyun.
The takeover means the group has completed its control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the source added.
 
 
Neither the Houthis nor the Yemeni government had officially commented on the reported takeover as of 1030GMT.
Perim Island holds exceptional strategic importance because of its location in the middle of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, where it divides the waterway into two channels.
 
The takeover is likely to heighten regional and international concerns over maritime security and the movement of commercial vessels and energy tankers through Bab al-Mandab.
 
In the same context, the source said the Houthis had seized Dhubab in Taiz province, prompting Yemeni government forces to withdraw to the southwestern province of Lahij.
 
Dhubab is a coastal city overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, and its capture strengthens Houthi control over the strategic waterway.
 
The strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and is one of the world’s most important routes for international trade and energy shipments.
 
The Houthis seized the entire western province of Al-Hudaydah after entering Hays and Al-Khawkhah. They also advanced through the western Taiz province and captured Red Sea coastal cities, including Mokha, extending their reach to the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
 
Government forces, meanwhile, made advances in the northern Al-Jawf province and moved closer to Al-Hazm, the provincial capital, while clashes continued on fronts in Marib, Al-Bayda and Al-Dhale provinces.
 
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014. A Saudi-led Arab coalition intervened in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government.

TAIEX retreats as investors rotate out of large-cap AI shares
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:35:26 UTC
19:35:26 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan’s benchmark stock index pulled back on Friday as large-cap stocks came under pressure.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Index, or TAIEX, closed down 755.64 points, or 1.61%, at 46,184.85. Turnover fell to NT$721.9 billion (US$22.8 billion), compared with NT$940 billion on Monday, according to Taiwan Index Plus and CTEE.
For the week, the TAIEX lost 366.28 points, or 0.79%. Total market capitalization of listed companies stood at NT$151.02 trillion, according to the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
All of the index’s most heavily weighted stocks ended lower. TSMC dropped 1.63% to NT$2,410.
MediaTek fell 2.86% to NT$4,625, while Foxconn lost 1.2% to NT$248. Delta Electronics declined 3.28% to NT$1,620, and ASE fell 4.92% to NT$618, according to Yahoo Stocks.
Chip designer AIchip Technologies fell to its daily limit-down at NT$3,650 despite reporting record-high revenue for August. Investors were concerned that Qualcomm’s partnership with Amazon Web Services to develop customized chips could take orders away from AIchip.
In the passive components sector, market leader Yageo fell 4.9%, while Walsin Technology lost 6.74%. Viking Tech, however, hit its daily limit-up as expectations for demand from the automotive and high-frequency markets supported trading volume, according to FTNN.
Software and information stocks were relatively resilient. Azion and Fortune Information Systems both closed at their daily limits, while Acer E-Enabling Service Business and Dimension Computer Technology also moved higher.
Funds also focused on the co-packaged optics and optoelectronic inspection sectors. FitTech and Unique Opto-Electronics both hit their daily limits.
Some non-electronics stocks benefited from expectations for more semiconductor plant construction and upgrades to AI inspection systems. Industrial filtration company Bright Sheland International and automation equipment maker Anderson Industrial both hit limit-ups, according to Sinotrade.
Container shipping stocks attracted funds seeking shelter from market volatility. Yang Ming Marine Transport gained 2.41%, Evergreen Marine rose 1.52%, and Wan Hai Lines added 1.36%, according to Sinotrade.
Analysts expect the TAIEX to continue fluctuating above its 20-day moving average, with investors rotating between sectors as external uncertainties persist. They said investors are likely to focus on US inflation data and rate signals from the Federal Reserve.
The market will also be sensitive to whether high-priced AI and semiconductor stocks stabilize and whether funds continue to move into oil- and raw material-related stocks. Analysts recommend buying on weakness rather than chasing prices, with stock selection focused on liquid large- and mid-cap AI stocks.

Russia's foreign recruit drive amounts to human trafficking, Amnesty International says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:34:33 UTC
19:34:33 KST

In a new report, human rights advocates say that in many cases the recruitment of foreigners into Russia's army amounts to the crime of human trafficking.
Russia is illegally recruiting foreign nationals into its military by using deception, blackmail, document confiscation and the threat of deportation to coerce migrants into fighting in Ukraine — a practice that amounts to human trafficking under international law, Amnesty International said in a report Thursday.
The finding follows interviews with prisoners of war from more than a dozen countries held in Ukrainian captivity, almost all of whom described abuses during recruitment that brought them into Russia's armed forces.
Practices documented by Amnesty International — including contracts signed without informed consent, confiscated passports, restricted freedom of movement, inadequate training and threats against those who tried to leave — meet the threshold for human trafficking under the UN Palermo Protocol, the organisation said.
The Palermo Protocol, or UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, defines human trafficking as the recruitment, transport or receipt of people through force, deception or coercion for the purpose of exploitation.
It is the primary international legal instrument on trafficking and has been ratified by 178 states, including Russia.
By April, Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War had identified 28,391 foreign nationals from 136 countries as having fought in Russia's armed forces. The figure excludes North Korean troops, who joined Russian forces at the front at the end of 2024.
Pyongyang deployed an estimated 10,000 troops to support Russian forces in late 2024, according to South Korean and US intelligence assessments, the first confirmed deployment of a third country's conventional military forces to the war.
Amnesty International sent a request for comment to Russian authorities and received no reply.
In May 2025, Russia designated it an "undesirable organisation," a legal classification that bans its presence in Russia, criminalises its activities in the country and prevents it from openly collecting information there.
How the recruitment works
Outside Russia, recruitment is built on deception. The most common scheme involves fake civilian job offers — in logistics, warehouses or construction — at salaries of around $2,000 a month.
Others promise help obtaining legal passage to the EU, presenting Russia as a transit country. Once people arrive, their documents are taken.
A third method exploits language barriers: foreign nationals sign what they believe is a civilian employment contract but find they have signed a contract with Russia's Defence Ministry.
Inside Russia, the methods shift to coercion. Labour migrants with irregular registration status and refugees are targeted specifically.
People detained for immigration violations are offered a choice between immediate deportation — which for many means poverty, persecution or danger at home — and signing a military contract.
The Russian authorities also operate through criminal human-trafficking networks and local intermediaries, Amnesty International said.
Amnesty International interviewed prisoners of war from Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, Egypt, Sierra Leone, Sri Lanka, Somalia and South Africa.
One of the most widely reported cases is that of Kenyan long-distance runner Evans Kibet, who travelled to Russia for a sporting event and said he was offered a civilian job before being taken to a training camp.
His documents and phone were confiscated after he signed a contract he said he did not understand, and he was sent to the front in Ukraine's Kharkiv region. He surrendered to Ukrainian forces in July 2025.
By recruiting foreign nationals, the Kremlin is also pursuing a domestic political objective: deaths among foreign recruits generate less public reaction inside Russia than Russian casualties, reducing pressure for a new mobilisation wave.
International reaction
A number of governments have lodged formal protests and demanded repatriation. India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Ghana, Jordan, South Africa and Botswana have all submitted diplomatic notes or official demands.
Criminal cases have been opened in several countries against local recruitment networks.
Cuba's government described the practice as human trafficking. In March, Kenya's Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi travelled to Moscow for urgent talks.
Russia subsequently promised to stop recruiting Kenyan citizens, withdraw surviving Kenyans from the combat zone and repatriate the bodies of those killed.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Saturday that Russia intended to return Indian citizens serving in its military "as soon as their identities are established."
On 12 March, the European Parliament voted by a majority to adopt a resolution formally defining Russia's recruitment of foreign nationals as human trafficking and grave human rights violations.

‘Lithuanian basketball has become a joke’: what’s happening to the country's main sport?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:34:00 UTC
19:34:00 KST

Lithuanian basketball is going through a crisis – the men's national team is struggling in its World Cup qualifiers, while the responsible Lithuanian Basketball Association is facing fierce criticism over the results as well as its handling of a sexual harassment scandal.
On Wednesday, LRT TV hosted a discussion examining the problems facing Lithuanian basketball. Participants included Mindaugas Balčiūnas, president of the Lithuanian Basketball Association, Eimantas Skersis, director of Utenos Juventus club, Justas Kalinauskas, secretary general of LTU Aquatics who also works for FIBA, Panevėžys Lietkabelis player Gabrielius Maldūnas, and basketball expert Ignas Grinevičius.
Jonas Miklovas, head of the Basketballnews website, was also due to take part, but Balčiūnas refused to participate if Miklovas was involved.
Following the programme, Balčiūnas announced on Friday he would be stepping down as the president of the basketball association.
Abuse scandal
In February last year, Lithuanian basketball was rocked by a scandal when women's national team players anonymously spoke about the inappropriate behaviour and psychological abuse they had experienced from then-head coach Rimantas Grigas.
The Lithuanian Basketball Association's Disciplinary, Ethics and Appeals Commission investigation took three days. It concluded that the players' testimonies contained no evidence of sexual harassment. Meanwhile, an investigation launched by FIBA lasted a year and a half.
On September 4, FIBA published its findings, banning R. Grigas from all basketball-related activities until October 27, 2030.
Following FIBA's findings, Balčiūnas also commented on the case, saying he regretted "the earlier assessment of the situation and the experiences suffered by the basketball players". He also discussed the issue during the programme.
"It is an especially painful moment. I have to acknowledge it once again and apologise for the initial inaccurate assessment. Clearly, the mechanisms for dealing with such a situation are new to us as an association and to Lithuania.
"Such cases probably had not occurred in Lithuanian basketball before, and our experience in dealing with such situations is very different from FIBA's because of the human, formal and legal mechanisms involved. Our regulations, even those governing collegial bodies and commissions, do not allow us to impose penalties of this scale.
"We can see that the initial situation was almost a matter for the Criminal Code, whereas we never claimed to have the authority to assess certain provisions of the Criminal Code. That is why we knew FIBA would take over the investigation. [...] We simply did not have the opportunity to interview the players in person. To this day, we do not know a single detail or person [involved]. FIBA had completely different tools at its disposal; it applied them and imposed sanctions," the association's president said.
Balčiūnas added that he respected FIBA's decision and regarded the situation as a "huge lesson for the entire basketball system".
The Lithuanian swimming community found itself in a similar situation. In December last year, swimmer Smiltė Plytnykaitė spoke out about harassment by coach Paulius Andrijauskas. He denied the allegations.
LTU Aquatics launched an investigation which lasted several months. Its findings, published at the end of March this year, established that the coach had breached professional ethics and disciplinary rules.
"We should emphasise the scale and importance of this investigation. For us as an association, it was something new. We knew how we should act, and we had basketball as a good example of how not to behave," Kalinauskas, secretary general of LTU Aquatics who also works for FIBA, said on the programme.
"My qualifications would allow me to assess the case quite clearly. I was a member of FIBA's World Legal Commission; I understand the processes, and judging by what the president of Lithuanian basketball is saying, I can say that this is, at the very least, a lie and a lack of competence," he said.
Skersis, director of the Utenos Juventus basketball club, also commented on the situation. According to him, there had already been talk within Lithuanian basketball about Grigas's inappropriate behaviour, and he compared the association's investigation to a lie.
"Anyone who is even remotely connected to basketball has known about this story for a long time. Yes, perhaps not the specific details, but everyone knew, more or less, that certain bad things were happening. To say that we carried out an investigation and found nothing is an absolute lie.
"I don't remember FIBA ever imposing a punishment of this scale on a coach. The association issued a statement, and Mindaugas himself apologised, so the facts are indisputable. Otherwise, you would have appealed rather than rushing to apologise. I don't understand how you could not have seen those facts when investigating the case in the commission. It is physically impossible. Either you are covering for a colleague, a long-time associate, or you are lying," Skersis said.
Although he did not take part in the programme, Miklovas, director of the Basketballnews basketball portal, later commented on the situation to LRT, calling the harassment scandal shameful and saying that Balčiūnas himself could have prevented it several years ago.
"It became even more shameful after basketball player Amalija Pašajevaitė revealed on Facebook that she had spoken to Balčiūnas and shared that sensitive information with him. According to Amalija, that conversation ended with an offer to have some green tea.
"That was the 2022–23 season, which means Balčiūnas had that information for at least two years. The question is how many other such conversations he had with various basketball players, and why he took no action after hearing the information.
“The following season, after Grigas had worked at the Aistės club, the federation promoted his appointment at Vilnius Kibirkštis. [...] Balčiūnas, having received that information from a basketball player, not only took no action but continued to promote that coach and placed him at that club.
"Three months later, the players, having had enough of his actions, his way of communicating and his overall behaviour, kicked him out. This is one of the very rare cases in basketball history where players – men or women – have dismissed a coach. And not because of results, but because of his behaviour. Did any warning lights go on then? No.
"Balčiūnas still did nothing. He only started doing something when the whole thing became public. When we talk about how new bodies are now being established and an entire system is being created to meet FIBA's requirements, let's stop and go back to 2022–23, when you did nothing to prevent this from happening. Why should we now believe you will do the right thing?" Miklovas said.
From glory to a laughing stock
In the World Cup qualifiers, the men’s national team coached by Rimas Kurtinaitis has won four games and lost four, and currently sits fourth in Group J. Only three teams from the group will qualify for the World Cup.
"The men's national team's results – we can look at the 2023 and 2025 championships – are the best they have been in a decade. The trajectory is upwards, apart from that loss to Italy, which was certainly very painful. And look at the talent coming through – Kasparas Jakučionis, Matas Buzelis, Motiejus Krivas, Matas Vokietaitis. If we had a fit Rokas Jokubaitis today, this discussion would not be happening," Balčiūnas said, discussing the national team's results.
Most of the criticism began after Lithuania suffered a heavy defeat by Italy in the qualifying window in July, despite having players such as Buzelis, Jakučionis and Valančiūnas in the squad.
After that window, Kurtinaitis resigned as head coach. However, after the Lithuanian Basketball Association failed to find a replacement, he continued in the role in August.
"Balčiūnas certainly knew what the players thought after that first summer window, because Dominykas Domarkas called the players, spoke to them and asked for their views on how the whole process within the national team had looked. And he certainly heard more than one opinion that the process was poorly organised, the preparation was very poor, the players did not know their roles, and the tactics were outdated or essentially did not exist.
"After hearing all that, they decided to look for a new coach. The fact that a new coach did not emerge and they were unable to find anyone again signals that Balčiūnas is incapable of running the federation. You are unable to replace a coach – that has never happened before. He failed to replace the coach because people refused to work with him. He only approached a few people, and we know that he cannot even speak to the top coaches. For example, I doubt they have had any contact with Šarūnas Jasikevičius.
"There are many areas where Balčiūnas is failing, but he hides behind the best results of the past 10 years. At the same time, we have a coach, Kurtinaitis, who used to say that anything below first place was last place. We have these contradictions," Miklovas said.
During Lithuania's most recent qualifying match in Vilnius against Bosnia and Herzegovina, fans held up a banner addressing the president of the association: "Balčiūnas, if the love is gone, leave basketball to those who love it."
"All the best players came to the June window this summer, which means everything was fine. There was disappointment with the result, emotional disappointment, and we acknowledge that,” the president of the Lithuanian Basketball Association said on the programme.
“The game against Italy was certainly not managed well, and that affected certain relationships. It is our responsibility, and my responsibility, to restore them now. As for some players not coming to the August window, we knew who would not come and why. We have to respect the players,
"Reality is different from before, when the national team came together once a year and everyone looked forward to it. Now it is four times a year: one window ends, and we already have to plan the next. Players get tired of one another and of the process, and these are human circumstances.
"Our work needs to be measured against sporting, economic and social criteria. The sporting results of all the national teams are at their highest level in a decade, despite that defeat. The budget is the largest in the organisation's history. [...] Solving problems is my responsibility. We need to address them, not run away from them," he said.
Skersis called for a broader view of the problems and questioned why the prestige of the Lithuanian national team had fallen so far.
"We are all discussing results, but the situation is somewhat different. The Lithuanian national basketball team is the tip of the iceberg. It is our country's pride, something we grew up watching. Look at what we have now.
"We have players where it is not the coaches choosing the best players and making the selection. Instead, we have players who simply turn up. In the coaching staff, we do not have the best coach, someone who would consider it an honour to coach the national team and would be its standard-bearer, like Jonas Kazlauskas or Dainius Adomaitis.
“Instead, we have people who are simply available – I'm talking about the assistants. When the head coach does not know the names of his assistants at a press conference, there is a problem.
"The entire pinnacle of the Lithuanian basketball pyramid, which we grew up with and looked forward to as if it were a celebration, has now become a laughing stock.
"How many tickets did you sell for the game against Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm not counting the complimentary tickets you gave away. [...] Nobody cares any more – or rather, everyone cares, but nobody wants to watch what you have turned basketball into during these years in charge. If a player or coach does not want to come, that is an organisational problem, because the organisation has no reputation," the Juventus director said.
Lithuania's qualification for the World Cup could be decided as early as the November or February qualifying windows. According to Grinevičius, the situation is not yet hopeless, while failing to reach the World Cup would also bring financial losses.
"I would rather look at the problems that could arise and try to get ahead of them. Strategically, as a basketball community, we need to answer how we are going to qualify for the World Cup, how we are going to put together the strongest possible squad and how we are going to have the best possible coaching and preparation. Otherwise, we risk having two years without basketball, apart from qualifiers and qualifiers for qualifiers.
"The basketball community needs to find a way to make the most of its potential, because state funding would probably also suffer significantly. In addition, we would not have broadcasts of the national team's major games. We should already be addressing this problem," the basketball expert said.
Lithuania's next World Cup qualifying match will be on November 26, when it hosts Serbia. Three days later, the national team will travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Both matches will be broadcast by LRT.

EU approves funding for Patriot missiles for Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:34:00 UTC
19:34:00 KST

EU approves funding for Patriot missiles for Ukraine
EU Commissioner for Defense and Space Andrius Kubilius said this at a press conference in Brussels on Friday, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
"Today, the Commission officially also approved EUR 6.1 billion for Ukraine air defense drones and missiles from the Ukraine Support Loan. This is really a very important step forward. We worked a lot with member states and Ukraine to this goal," the commissioner said.
He stressed that the decision is a crucial step toward ensuring the Ukrainian military's combat capability and protecting critical infrastructure from Russian attacks.
According to the official, the decision will allow Ukraine to urgently address shortages of precision weapons and missiles for Patriot air defense systems through exemptions from the general procurement rules.
"The decision officially enables Ukraine to procure PAC-3 missiles for Patriots. Funded under the Ukraine Support Loan, the package includes five derogations from standard eligibility conditions – three for Ukrainian-made drones and components exceeding cost thresholds and two for U.S.-made equipment, in particular PAC-3 missiles, including we as a NATO-coordinated portal mechanism," Kubilius said.
The EU commissioner noted that the speed of deliveries is now a decisive factor, and that the partnership between the EU and Ukraine should ensure a steady supply of the weapons needed on the battlefield.
"Ukraine's military edge depends on the rapid availability of critical products in the required quantities and within very short time frames. Accelerating EU deliveries through desk stocking, reprioritizing orders, and ramping up the production remains crucial," he said.
Asked about the timeline for the delivery of PAC-3 missiles, Kubilius stressed that allies are looking for flexible solutions to immediately meet Ukraine's needs until new batches leave the factory.
He said the question now was whether it is possible to reach agreements with member states that already have PAC-3 missiles in their stockpiles to transfer these missiles from their stocks to Ukraine now and then receive replacements under Ukraine's agreements for 2027.
As reported, under the approved decision, the European Union has fully allocated the EUR 28.3 billion planned for this year to finance Ukraine's defense under the Ukraine Support Loan.
The European Commission is currently processing a request for the disbursement of another EUR 4.7 billion tranche, after EUR 8.3 billion had already been transferred.
According to European Commission estimates, Ukraine's annual needs to defend against ballistic attacks amount to around 2,000 PAC-3 interceptor missiles for Patriot systems, while global production capacity is only gradually increasing, requiring flexible solutions from NATO and EU allies.

Ukrainian-designed drones to be manufactured in Canada with General Dynamics
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher

13:34:00 EEST

Ukrainian-designed drones to be manufactured in Canada with General Dynamics
Ukrainian drone developer GreenTech Harvest has reached an agreement with Canadian defence giant General Dynamics Mission Systems-Canada to jointly produce drones in Canada.
Source: a press release by General Dynamics
Details: The two parties signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU).
The company reported that under the memorandum the two firms have established a framework for cooperation focused on Ukrainian-designed unmanned systems.
"By working together, we can combine that experience with our Canadian industrial and manufacturing expertise to help deliver capability where it is needed while strengthening defence cooperation between our countries," said Joel Houde, vice president and general manager of General Dynamics Mission Systems-Canada.
More details: According to Oleh Donets, Programme Director at GreenTech Harvest, the two companies aim to combine combat-tested drones with the Canadian firm's capabilities to produce systems and solutions that will strengthen the defence capabilities of both countries.
For reference: GreenTech Harvest is a Ukrainian manufacturer of unmanned systems. The company is one of nine Ukrainian founding members of the EU-Ukraine Drone Alliance, which the European Commission launched in July 2026.
In April, GreenTech Harvest agreed with the Dutch VDL Group to jointly manufacture drones at a plant in Born. This concerns the K4 Deepstrike attack drone and the Midstrike Plane Baton reconnaissance drone.
Background: In May, Ukrainian company Airlogix and Canadian manufacturer Sentinel Research and Development established the Airlogix-Sentinel joint venture to produce drones in Canada, with support from the governments of both countries.

Türkiye mediates between rival Libya groups in Ankara
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:33:38 UTC
19:33:38 KST

Ibrahim Kalın, head of the National Intelligence Organization (MİT) (right), met with Akile Salih, Speaker of the Libyan House of Representatives (center), and Muhammad Takala, Chairman of the High State Council (left). AA photo.
Ankara has stepped up its mediation efforts between Libya’s rival Tripoli and Benghazi administrations, quietly hosting reconciliation talks in the Turkish capital to foster national unity and stability.
According to security sources, National Intelligence Organization (MIT) President İbrahim Kalın met Aguila Saleh, the speaker of Libya’s House of Representatives, and Mohammed Takala, the president of Libya’s High Council of State (HSC), on late September 10 in Ankara.
Saleh represents the eastern administration based in Benghazi under the leadership of General Khalifa Hafter and Takala has recently been re-elected as the head of the HSC in Tripoli under the U.N.-recognized Government of National Unity (GNU) led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh.
The talks in Ankara followed an agreement reached by the two rival camps, dubbed the 4+4 agreement, which outlines concrete steps toward institutional unification and the realization of national elections.
A North African country, known for its rich carbon reserves, has been divided since 2014. Türkiye supported the Tripoli-based, UN-recognized government since 2019 but has recently developed good relations with Benghazi as well. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan’s recent visit to Libya did cover both administrations and aimed to foster ties between the two countries.
According to sources, the talks in Ankara addressed recent developments in Libya and the region, the political and military unification of Libya, and steps that need to be taken for further improvement of the Türkiye-Libya relationship.
The meeting also addressed achieving permanent progress on issues that have remained unresolved for a long time and reaching a broad consensus among all parties, sources stated.
The sources informed that Saleh and Takala agreed on the goals of ensuring political unity in the entirety of Libya while emphasizing the leading roles of the HSC and the House of Representatives.
The meeting in Ankara injected fresh hopes for overcoming standing obstacles in front of holding presidential and national elections and reaching a fully unified government in Libya.
Sources recalled that the meeting in Ankara is considered highly significant, as it marks the first time the heads of the two institutions came together in Türkiye to discuss these issues and made concrete progress on processes that had been at a deadlock.

Americans have occupied all the spots in the top 10 richest people in the world for the first time
Kyiv • UNN
Bernard Arnault dropped out of the top ten richest people due to a $65 billion decline in his fortune. For the first time, the ranking was completely dominated by Americans, led by Musk.
French luxury-goods magnate Bernard Arnault has dropped out of the world’s ten richest people, giving way in a ranking that now consists entirely of Americans, mostly technology billionaires. Bloomberg reports, writes UNN.
Details
It is noted that French luxury magnate Bernard Arnault, the founder of Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy (LVMH), lost his place in the top ten, with his fortune falling below that of American investor Warren Buffett.
Elon Musk leads the list by a wide margin, with a fortune of $918.8 billion. He is followed by technology entrepreneurs, including Larry Page, Jeff Bezos, Sergey Brin and Michael Dell. For the first time since the wealth index was launched in 2012, all ten top positions are held by Americans.
Arnault’s decline in wealth has been particularly noticeable since the beginning of the year. The 77-year-old billionaire’s fortune has fallen by $65 billion—the largest drop among the world’s 500 richest people. The war in the Middle East has severely hit his business, reducing demand in shopping hubs such as Dubai for LVMH brands—from clothing makers Dior, Louis Vuitton and Tiffany to premium alcohol, including Dom Perignon champagne and Hennessy cognac. The company has also faced difficulties in China, a key market for it, where a trademark dispute with a local tea producer has negatively affected sales.
Shares of LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE rose 0.5% in Friday morning trading in Paris. The previous day, the company briefly lost its status as France’s largest company by market capitalization to L’Oreal SA.
Meanwhile, the U.S. stock index S&P 500 has risen 11% since the beginning of the year, driven to a significant extent by technology companies amid demand related to artificial intelligence.
Arnault had been among the world’s ten richest people since March 22, 2017, and briefly held the top position starting in December 2022. He was the first person from outside North America—and the only representative of the consumer-goods industry—to top the ranking. Since then, no one has managed to repeat this achievement.

Finland becomes industrial addendum of Ukrainian military — opposition politician
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-11
10:30:55 UTC
19:30:55 KST

MOSCOW, September 11. /TASS/. Finland has become one of the key platforms for the localization of Ukrainian defense technologies, evolving into an industrial extension of Ukraine’s military-industrial complex, according to Viktor Medvedchuk, leader of the Other Ukraine movement and former head of the Opposition Platform - For Life party, which has been banned in Ukraine.
"Finland is turning into an industrial extension of the Ukrainian military-industrial complex. In the three years since joining NATO, Finland - which shares a 1,340-kilometer border with Russia - has evolved from an arms supplier to Ukraine into one of the most important hubs for the localization, production, and integration of Ukrainian defense technologies into Finnish industrial infrastructure," Medvedchuk wrote in an article published on the movement’s website.
"By autumn 2026, this is expected to develop into an extensive network of joint ventures and production facilities covering virtually the entire spectrum of modern drone warfare. This expanded military-industrial infrastructure is being used to support strikes against civilian and military targets inside Russian territory," he added.
